deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no derivation. It is a bibliographic list of titles, in Latin, French and German, separated by horizontal rules. The note at the end shows these are writings of Leonhard Euler. Gauss was probably copying from a published catalogue of Euler's works, such as the one appended to N. Fuss's Éloge of 1783/86.

(1) 'Observationes circa integralia formularum ∫x^{p-1}dx(1-x^n)^{q/n-1} posito post integrationem x=1'. This is Euler's paper E321 (Novi Commentarii Acad. Petrop. 16, 1771/72). In modern terms it studies the definite integral ∫_0^1 x^{p-1}(1-x^n)^{(q-n)/n} dx = (1/n)·B(p/n, q/n). It also studies Euler's product relations among such integrals, which are equivalent to Gamma-function identities. On this page the exponent is written as (q-n)/n, or perhaps (q-1)/n, and the base appears as (1-x). The superscript n on x is either faint or omitted in the copy.

(2) 'Mémoires de la Société de Flessingue (Vlissingen), Tome IX, 1782: Recherches sur une nouvelle espèce de quarrés magiques'. This is Euler's E530 on orthogonal Latin squares, including the 36-officers problem.

(3) 'Ephemerides de Berlin 1783 [Berliner Astronomisches Jahrbuch]: Theorie der Parallaxen für die sphäroidische Gestalt der Erde'. This is an Euler contribution on computing parallax for the spheroidal Earth.

(4) 'Mémoires de la Société Économique [probably Bern], VI, 1766: Nachricht von einem neuen Mittel zur Vermehrung des Getraides' (a notice of a new means of increasing grain yield). It is listed among Euler items; the attribution is unsure.

(5) The final note reads roughly: '208 treatises [exist] in manuscript, of which however 13 are already printed in the second volume of the Opuscula [analytica, 1785] and very many in the Nova Acta'. This refers to Euler's posthumous papers, which the St Petersburg Academy published progressively in the Nova Acta.

Nothing is computed. The page records Gauss's reading notes or a bibliographic excerpt about Euler's work.
errors: 'cira' should be 'circa'. This is a slip in the manuscript, or a copying abbreviation.

Euler's integrand is x^{p-1}(1-x^n)^{q/n-1}. The page seems to read (1-x)^{(q-n)/n}, so the power n on x is missing or illegible. Without it the exponent (q-n)/n gives a Beta function B(p,q/n), not Euler's normalised form. This is most likely a copying slip or the transcription missing a faint n.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely a bibliographic excerpt listing Euler's works and his posthumous manuscripts. It contains no mathematics of Gauss's own. Gauss's close reading of Euler is well documented.

checkable.asserts: Euler's integral equals (1/n)·B(p/n,q/n) for p=3, q=4, n=2 (should be 0).
With base (1-x) as apparently written, the integral is B(p,q/n) instead (here p=2, q=3, n=1).

transcription_corrections: Line 1: the manuscript has 'cira' (a slip for 'circa'). The transcription's 'talium formularum' matches the image.
Integrand: the image likely intends (1-x^n)^{(q-n)/n}, per Euler's title. The exponent of x in the base is not visible or is omitted.
'Societeit' is a mixed Dutch/French form in the manuscript, read as 'Société de Vlissingue'. 'quarres' continues across the line break as 'quar-res'.
German line under Ephemerides: read as 'Theorie der Parallaxen für die sphäroidische Gestalt der Erde'. The handwriting is cursive and the reading is plausible.

Last paragraph: the first word reads like 'Ange' or 'Ausser' rather than clearly 'Anzahl'; the reading is uncertain. The rest is '208 Abh. in Manuscript wovon indess 13 schon im zweiten Bande der Opuscul. u. sehr viele in den Novis actis abgedruckt sind.'
A folio number '3' is written in the right margin.
